messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
I'm after roughly 650 m of altitude. Motor no bigger than 38 mm. Has to land softer than 15 ft/s.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: Apogee roughly 650 m, so about 650 m, within 5%. Motor diameter at most 38 mm, which is 0.038 m (maximum). Landing softer than 15 ft/s. 15 * 0.3048 = 4.57 m/s, so touchdown must stay under that (maximum). Wind, rail and site are not stated: I assume 2 m/s wind, a vertical 1.5 m rail and sea level. Single stage, no payload and no duration cap.

2. Feasibility: Drag-free speed for 650 m is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 650) = 113 m/s. A 29 mm G will usually fall short of that once drag is included, and a light 38 mm I will sail past it. An H in a modest 38 mm airframe is the band I want. Looking up a few H and I motors in that diameter before sizing.

2. Feasibility: Every one of those motors is 29 mm, which is inside the 38 mm cap. The H128W gives 178 N*s and 153 N for 1.16 s, loaded mass 0.20 kg, and its only delay is 14 s. The H180W has 234 N*s but only a 6 s delay, which would open the chute while a 650 m flight is still climbing. The I200W is 327 N*s with a plugged delay and would overshoot a "roughly 650 m" target in any light airframe. The G80T at 136 N*s is the one most likely to fall short. I will build around the H128W and use its 14 s ejection.

3. Size: Guess liftoff mass 0.32 kg for a short 42 mm cardboard rocket plus the motor. Thrust-to-weight is 153 / (0.32 * 9.81) = 48.7. Weight is 0.32 * 9.81 = 3.14 N, so rail acceleration is (153 - 3.14) / 0.32 = 468 m/s^2 and rail exit is about sqrt(2 * 468 * 1.5) = 37.5 m/s. Burnout mass is 0.32 - 0.094 = 0.226 kg. To descend at 4 m/s, under the 4.57 m/s cap, canopy area is 2 * 0.226 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 4^2) = 0.283 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.283 / 3.1416) = 0.600 m. A 0.70 m chute gives some margin because "softer than 15 ft/s" has no slack.

4. Draft: 42 mm cardboard tube, 0.50 m long, hollow polystyrene ogive, three balsa fins, 29 mm mount for the H128W-14. Checking it on the default 1.5 m rail and 2 m/s wind.

4. Check: The simulator gives 1174.9 m, far above a roughly 650 m target. 5% either side of 650 m is about 618 to 683 m, and 1174.9 m is not in that band. Stability fails too: 0.23 cal at rail exit, and 0.23 cal is also the minimum during the burn, against a 1.0 cal floor. Landing 3.4 m/s is under the 4.57 m/s cap, rail exit 41.1 m/s and thrust-to-weight 49.3 are fine, and the motor is 29 mm. The 14 s delay opened the chute at 15.3 s, about 4 s after the 11.38 s apogee, at 14.7 m/s. Liftoff mass is 0.316 kg, almost exactly the guess, so the miss is too little drag rather than a bad mass estimate. Peak Mach is 1.27.

5. Fix: The failing stability value is 0.23 cal, limit 1.0, and the altitude miss is the same small fin set. One change: four balsa fins with root 0.13 m, tip 0.045 m and span 0.08 m. That should push the CP back and add the drag this light H128 airframe is missing. Motor, chute and tube stay the same.

4. Check: Larger fins fixed stability. The simulator gives 1.25 cal at rail exit and through the burn, over the 1.0 cal floor. Apogee is still high: 907.6 m against roughly 650 m. (907.6 - 650) / 650 = 40% high, outside the 5% band. Landing 3.5 m/s stays under 4.57 m/s, rail exit is 40.2 m/s and thrust-to-weight is 47.7. The 14 s delay is now a real problem: apogee is at 9.97 s and the chute opens at 15.3 s already doing 37.4 m/s. That is a warning, not the missed target.

5. Fix: The failing value is apogee 907.6 m, and the target is roughly 650 m. The fin drag already took a bite out of 1174.9 m; the next lever is mass, placed in the nose so the 1.25 cal margin does not go backwards. One change: 0.20 kg of clay at the top of the tube. That is 0.20 / 0.326 = 61% more than the 0.326 kg liftoff mass. I am not counting on a full 61% altitude cut, only on moving toward the band. The late ejection stays for this flight so I can see the mass effect on its own.

messages.reasoning_content:
4. Check: The clay went the wrong way. The simulator gives 1085.8 m, higher than the 907.6 m of the lighter rocket, and still nowhere near 650 m. Peak Mach fell from 1.07 to 0.86, so the extra mass walked it out of the transonic drag rise and the coast got easier. Stability is now 4.1 cal, rail exit 31.9 m/s, thrust-to-weight 29.6. Landing rose to 4.7 m/s, which is over the 4.57 m/s cap. The chute still opens late, at 15.3 s and 27.8 m/s, after apogee at 12.29 s.

5. Fix: Both failing numbers, 1085.8 m and 4.7 m/s, come from hauling an H's impulse with a mass that is no longer fast enough to throw that impulse away as drag. Less mass made it worse, so the impulse has to come down. I am looking up F and G motors, still at or under 29 mm, before I throw out the H128W and the clay.

5. Fix: G64W is 118 N*s, about 118 / 178 = 0.66 of the H128W, burned over 1.92 s at 61 N, mass 0.15 kg, with an 8 s delay. F40W at 78 N*s would likely fall through the bottom of the band, and the G77R at 100 N*s has less margin on thrust. The clay comes out: it raised apogee and pushed landing to 4.7 m/s. Airframe mass from the last two flights is 0.526 - 0.20 - 0.202 = 0.124 kg, so a G64W liftoff is 0.124 + 0.151 = 0.275 kg. Thrust-to-weight is 61 / (0.275 * 9.81) = 22.6, rail acceleration (61 - 2.70) / 0.275 = 212 m/s^2, rail exit sqrt(2 * 212 * 1.5) = 25.2 m/s. The four large fins stay, since they were what got the margin from 0.23 cal to 1.25 cal, and a lighter motor moves the CG forward from there. Delay is 8 s so ejection is near apogee instead of at 27.8 m/s.

4. Check: The simulator gives 842.8 m. Against roughly 650 m that is (842.8 - 650) / 650 = 30% high, still outside the 5% band. Everything else passes. Margin is 1.15 cal at rail exit and through the burn, rail exit is 34.3 m/s, thrust-to-weight is 22.5, landing is 3.3 m/s under the 4.57 m/s cap, and the motor is 29 mm. Ejection at 10.4 s is just after the 9.94 s apogee, at 4.8 m/s, with no warning. Liftoff mass is 0.276 kg.

5. Fix: third revision and the altitude still misses. 842.8 m remains above the band, so I am stopping rather than adding another guess. The design is otherwise inside the gates.

6. Uncertainty: This one stayed subsonic (Mach 0.76), so the drag model is less wild than the H128 flights, but apogee still moves a lot with fin area and with whether the coast is transonic. The 0.276 kg liftoff mass is a model value; a heavier build would come down toward 650 m, and a lighter one would go higher. Chute Cd is assumed 0.8. The 8 s delay only just matches apogee, so a slower build could open early.
messages.content:
G64W-8 in a 42 mm cardboard rocket, four balsa fins, 0.70 m chute on the motor ejection.
Safe flight: 1.15 cal margin, 34.3 m/s off the 1.5 m rail, landing 3.3 m/s.
Apogee still exceeds the roughly 650 m target. The simulator gives 842.8 m, outside the 5% band after three revisions.
